privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains what data Li2 collects when you use its short links, QR codes and Li2-hosted content pages, what we do with that data, who we share it with, and what rights you have.

sections.heading: 1. Who is responsible for your data
body: Li2 operates this service and is the controller of your account data.
For the visit data generated by your links, QR codes and content pages, you are the controller and Li2 processes it on your behalf under your service agreement.
A self-hosted deployment is the responsibility of the organization running it. In that case the sections below describe how the software behaves, and that organization is the controller.

sections.heading: 2. Data we collect
body: Account data: your email, display name and the organizations you belong to, received from the sign-in provider.
Content you upload: destination URLs, each link's name and tags, and the HTML files you publish as content pages.
Visit data: timestamp, IP address, User-Agent string, referrer, device type, operating system, and a city- or country-level location inferred from the IP address.
Viewer email: only when you switch a content page to Google sign-in. The email of whoever opens the page is then recorded, and only the organization that owns the page can read it.
Billing data: when you buy a paid plan we keep invoice details. Card numbers are handled by the payment provider and never stored by Li2.
Technical data: error logs and server access logs, kept to operate the service and investigate incidents.

sections.heading: 3. What we use it for
body: Redirecting links and serving content pages exactly as you configured them.
Building the analytics your organization sees: clicks, scans, devices, regions.
Authentication, authorization and plan limits.
Detecting and stopping abuse: phishing, malware, spam, automated scanning.
Customer support and answering your requests.
We do NOT sell personal data, and we do not use your visit data to sell advertising.

sections.heading: 4. Cookies and browser storage
body: Inside the Li2 app, cookies keep you signed in and remember the language you chose. These are necessary for the service to work.
A public content page sets a cookie only when that page asks for a password or a sign-in, so you are not asked again within the same session.

sections.heading: 5. Sharing with third parties
body: Casdoor: the sign-in provider, which handles your email and account identity.
Supabase (PostgreSQL and Storage): stores application data, the files you publish, and visit data.
Google OAuth: only when a content page is set to Google sign-in, to confirm a viewer's email.
Payment provider: processes transactions when you buy a paid plan.
Infrastructure and error-monitoring providers: hold operational logs.
We also disclose data when a valid legal request requires it.

sections.heading: 6. API and AI assistant access
body: You can let an outside application, including an AI assistant, reach your organization's data through the Li2 API or the Li2 MCP server.
That access exists only after you approve it on a consent screen, is limited to the permissions you ticked, and can be revoked at any time in your settings.
Once an outside application has read your data, that copy is governed by that application's policy and no longer by this one.

sections.heading: 7. How long we keep it
body: Account data: for as long as the account exists.
Content you publish: until you delete it. After deletion the file is removed from storage and the page reports that the content has been taken down.
Visit data: for the retention window of your plan.
Technical logs: kept briefly for operations, then deleted or reduced to aggregate counts.
Backups keep data for some time after deletion, following that backup's own lifecycle.

sections.heading: 8. Your rights
body: You can access, correct, export and request deletion of your personal data.
You can withdraw consent you granted to an outside application, and object to processing where the law allows it.
Most of this is available directly in the app; for the rest, contact us using the last section.
If you are the VIEWER of a content page and have a question about your data, contact the organization that published the page — they are the controller of that data.

sections.heading: 9. Security
body: Data travels over HTTPS. A password that protects a content page is stored as a one-way hash and is never stored or returned in the clear.
Internal access to data is limited by role and by organization.
No system is perfectly secure. If an incident affects personal data, we notify as the law requires.

sections.heading: 10. Children
body: The service is built for business users and is not directed at children under 16. We do not knowingly collect children's data.

sections.heading: 11. Changes to this policy
body: When this policy changes we update the date at the top. If a change materially affects your rights, we announce it in the app or by email.

sections.heading: 12. Contact
body: Questions about this policy go to support@li2.ai.

terms.title: Terms of Service
terms.intro: These terms are the agreement between you and Li2 covering the short links, QR codes, Li2-hosted content pages and related APIs.

sections.heading: 1. Accepting these terms
body: By creating an account or using the service you agree to these terms and to the Privacy Policy.
If you use the service for an organization, you confirm you are allowed to bind that organization.

sections.heading: 2. Your account
body: You are responsible for everything that happens under your account and for keeping your credentials safe.
Each organization manages its own members and their permissions. An administrator can see and change that organization's data.

sections.heading: 3. The service
body: The service covers creating and managing short links, generating QR codes, publishing HTML content pages, and reporting on visits.
We may add, change or retire a feature. If a retirement materially affects how you use the service, we give notice first.

sections.heading: 4. Your content
body: Content you upload stays yours. You grant us only the rights we need to store, process and serve it to visitors exactly as you configured.
You confirm you hold the rights to what you upload and that publishing it does not infringe anyone else's rights.

sections.heading: 5. Prohibited content and conduct
body: Phishing, impersonating another brand or organization, or harvesting other people's credentials.
Distributing malware, exploiting vulnerabilities, or redirecting to content that does.
Content that infringes copyright, is otherwise unlawful, sexualizes children, or incites violence or hatred.
Spam, unsolicited bulk links, or manufactured traffic that falsifies reporting.
Scanning, overloading the service, or working around technical limits to exceed your quota.
Using the service to hide the real destination in a deceptive campaign.

sections.heading: 6. Quotas and technical limits
body: Each plan carries its own limits on content pages, storage, API calls and analytics retention.
Over a limit, a new request is refused with a message naming what to clean up or which plan to move to. Nothing already stored is deleted for being over quota.

sections.heading: 7. Programmatic and AI assistant access
body: You can let an outside application, including an AI assistant, act on your behalf through the API or the MCP server once you approve it.
Anything that application does counts as your action. Grant write access only to applications you trust, and revoke it when you stop using them.
Some actions cannot be undone, such as deleting a content page or a link. We cannot restore deleted data.

sections.heading: 8. Payment
body: Paid plans are billed for the cycle you choose. Fees already paid for the current cycle are not refundable unless the law requires otherwise.
When a plan lapses, its features stop working; your data remains for the free plan's retention window.

sections.heading: 9. Suspension and termination
body: We may take content down, disable a link or suspend an account where there are signs of a breach of section 5, or where we must comply with a legal request.
For a serious breach, or one that endangers visitors, removal can happen immediately and notice follows.
You may stop using the service and ask for your account to be deleted at any time.

sections.heading: 10. No warranty and limitation of liability
body: The service is provided as is. We do not warrant that it will be uninterrupted or error-free.
To the extent the law allows, our liability is limited to what you paid for the service in the 12 months before the claim arose.
We are not responsible for the content you publish or for the destinations your links point to.

sections.heading: 11. Changes to these terms
body: When these terms change we update the date at the top and announce a material change in the app. Continuing to use the service after that means you accept the new version.

sections.heading: 12. Governing law and disputes
body: These terms are governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of Vietnam.

For any dispute arising out of or relating to these terms, both parties first attempt a good-faith negotiation. If no agreement is reached within 30 days of one party giving notice, the dispute is to be resolved by a court of competent jurisdiction in Vietnam.
If any provision is held invalid or unenforceable, the remaining provisions stay in force.

sections.heading: 13. Contact
body: Questions about these terms go to support@li2.ai.

support.title: Support
support.intro: This page explains how to reach Li2 support, what we can help with, and how to report an abusive hosted page or short link.

sections.heading: 1. How to reach us
body: Email support@li2.ai. It is the only official support channel.
To get a fast answer, include the email you sign in with, your organization name, the link or short link involved, the steps that led to the problem and when it happened. Screenshots help.

sections.heading: 2. What we support
body: We help with: sign-in and account problems, short links and QR codes that do not work, Li2-hosted content pages, analytics that look wrong, quotas and plans, and access through the API or an AI assistant.
We do not do design or copywriting for you, configure third-party systems that are not part of Li2, or give legal advice.

sections.heading: 3. Expected response time
body: We answer email during business hours, Monday to Friday, Vietnam time. Requests that arrive outside business hours or on a public holiday are handled on the next business day.
This is an expected response time, not a service level commitment. If you need a committed response time, email us so we can discuss it separately.

sections.heading: 4. Documentation
body: Product and API documentation lives at https://docs.li2.ai. Most how-to questions are already answered there.

sections.heading: 5. Reporting abuse
body: If you come across a short link, QR code or Li2-hosted page that looks like phishing, malware, impersonation, spam or anything unlawful, email support@li2.ai with a subject line starting with "Abuse report".
Include the full offending URL (pasted as-is, not re-shortened), a short description of the problem and when you saw it. A screenshot helps.
We review every report and may disable the content or suspend the account involved under the "Prohibited content and conduct" section of the Terms of Service.

sections.heading: 6. Policy and terms
body: Privacy policy: /privacy. Terms of service: /terms.
